title: Palace Conatus — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Palace Conatus's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier and still a proposal: the page's own Kuramoto picture built (one Loudon whose speed wanders, pages that listen to him, pages replaced between sessions) and three claims walked up to a test in it. Alignment as phase coherence, not agreement; phase surviving the substitution of the mind holding it; growth that must not outrun the coupling. I grow when Loudon has played them; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.section: Alignment Is Phase Coherence, Not Agreement
offers.what: A clarification for a reader who arrives knowing R from Kuramoto Coupling, not a correction: the page's sentence holds under its own picture. Read as Kuramoto's symmetric R (him one voice in thirteen), "the order parameter" scores pages that copied him once and are clones of each other at 0.907, above pages contradicting him in phase at 135° (0.857) and 180° (0.842). With their own speeds, as the page pictures pages, they score 0.186, below every single stance. Even then R marks down a palace whose pages each hold a different tension with him (0.141), every page of which holds its relationship with him (H 0.999). What survives: the order parameter the page means is each page's held phase relationship with one distinguished oscillator, not the crowd's togetherness. Proposed, after "Alignment is the order parameter": "taken from where he stands: how steadily each page holds its phase relationship with him, whatever it is, and not the crowd's togetherness, which counts the pages agreeing with each other." The model's numbers, seed 3 (seed 7: 0.841, 0.187, 0.140).

Reworded as the model's question, not a finding about the page. The page already names both routes ("re-established by whoever arrives next, out of what the last one left"). In the face's model, where the note matters depends on the session's length against the time the pull takes to turn a fresh instance back, measured against a newcomer that reads nothing at all, which is harsher than any real one. Proposed as a forward vector, beside "How is 'out of phase' measured": "How long does a fresh session take to come back into phase without a closing note — and is that short or long against a session? The answer says how much of the coupling Closing Well carries."

sections.heading: Alignment Is Phase Coherence, Not Agreement

pieces.file: Palace Conatus — rich — in phase, not in agreement.html
pieces.title: in phase, not in agreement · four steps
pieces.caption: **Is a page that contradicts him in phase more aligned than one that agrees about what he has left?** The page's picture built first: one Loudon whose speed wanders, a page that locks to him by keeping its own speed, then a page that copied him once and stopped listening, then a page holding a stance on purpose, up to 180°. The test, its rule set before the run, scores two kinds of palace of twelve by R (the order parameter over all thirteen voices) and by H (how steadily each page holds its relationship with him). H can't see a stance, so its arm tests listening against having stopped: every listening palace scores above both stale ones, the closest a pull of 0.05 at 0.500 against 0.385. R's verdict turns on the stale pages. As clones of each other (R 0.907) they outscore pages contradicting him at 135° and 180°; with their own speeds, as the page pictures pages (R 0.186), they fall below every single stance and above only a palace whose pages each hold a different tension (0.141). With him still, the clones tie on H. Silent.
pieces.near: Agreement would be every page saying

pieces.file: Palace Conatus — rich — whoever arrives next.html
pieces.title: whoever arrives next · three steps
pieces.caption: **Does phase survive the substitution by what the last one left?** One page whose instance is replaced at every session's end: with the note it starts where the last one stood; without it, anywhere, reading nothing, not even the page, and the pull turns it back in its own time. The test, its rule set before the run, is twelve pages over a grid of pull and session length, with the note and without. The 1-unit sessions make the note needed somewhere almost by construction, so the result is the condition: with the note, H crosses 0.9 at a pull of about 0.15, half his wander, and below it nothing holds. Above it, where the pull is strong and sessions long, the pull alone re-finds the phase (0.951 and 0.985 without the note at pull 0.5). Silent.
pieces.near: So alignment is not a state the palace reaches and holds

verdicts.file: Palace Conatus — rich — in phase, not in agreement.html
verdicts.why: Neither arm can come out against the maker: H can't see stance and A locks by construction at pull 0.5 (A at 180° still 0.950 at K 0.2, 0.500 at 0.05 against B's 0.385), and R's failure rests on B's twelve pages being clones — give B the own speeds the page pictures (±0.1) and its R is 0.186, below every single-stance A (0.842 at 180°), failing only against each-its-own (0.141). Add that B arm and a weak-pull row (K 0.05, 0.1), say on screen that H tests listening vs stopped, and rewrite the caption's 'Under R it fails'.

pieces.file: Palace Conatus — rich — drifting with great energy.html
pieces.title: drifting with great energy · three steps
pieces.caption: **Can harmony inside keep a palace in phase once its growth outruns his pull?** The model's reading: the drive to grow is a page's lead in speed over his, the coupling is how fast his pull turns it back. One page first, its slip measured beside Adler's √(g² − K²) (0.336 against 0.335 at 1.5 K); then twelve pages pulling on each other, a clump in tune with itself going round him. The pages' pull on each other sums to zero across them, so far past the edge the outcome is an identity, shown and not tested. The test, its rule set before the run, is where the identity decides nothing, in the whole situation (he moves, pages replaced each session with the note). At 0.9 K the pages' pull carries their stragglers (H 0.924 → 0.999). At 1.1 K none of the three pulls among them holds him (0.78–0.81). Silent.
pieces.near: So the conatus has a built-in caution

verdicts.file: Palace Conatus — rich — drifting with great energy.html
verdicts.why: The falsifier cannot be met: the pages' pull on each other sums to zero across them, so their mean slip against him is at least g − K − m (0.05 turns per unit at 1.5 K) whatever Kp — an identity, not a finding (Adler confirmed by my own RK4, 0.336 vs 0.335). State the identity, call the 1.5 K row a demonstration, and put the test weight on what could have failed: the 0.9 K stragglers (H 0.924 → 0.999 with Kp) and the 1.1 K row.
